Your current working directory is a scratch task directory; use it only for ./notes.md. Run repository commands with `cd /home/powerbox2/src/ringer-worktrees/shared-evidence && ...`.

OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY: you own only these repo paths: ringer.py, ringer_core/central_evidence.py, tests/test_central_evidence.py, tests/test_model_log.py, tests/test_eval_logger_central.py. Do not modify, create, delete, format or stage anything else. Do not run git add, git commit or git push. Do not install packages and do not add dependencies; the `psycopg` package is NOT installed here and all tests must pass without it (use fakes). Inside ringer.py you may edit ONLY the EvalLogger class (and, if truly needed, the import block at the top of the file); an automated check rejects any other ringer.py change. Do not change the RingerRunner logger interface: a logger is any object with log_attempt(row) and close().

STYLE: match the surrounding code (type hints, small methods, comment density like the neighbouring code, stdlib unittest). Make the simplest change that meets the brief; no extras.

READ FIRST (read-only): ringer.py class EvalLogger and parse_env_file; ringer_core/central_evidence.py (already written; you will make three small edits to it, listed below); ringer_core/config.py (PostgresEvalConfig now has env_file, spec_storage, source_host); tests/test_model_log.py (the test test_postgres_params_exclude_local_model_log_keys, which you will rewrite); tests/test_central_evidence.py; specs/002-shared-evidence/spec.md requirements R2, R3, R5, R6, R10, R12 for background. The instructions in THIS brief are authoritative.

GOAL: make EvalLogger write every attempt to the local JSONL file ALWAYS, and ALSO to the central Postgres table when a connection is configured ("dual-write"). Today it writes Postgres OR JSONL, with a 12-column insert that drops model, task_type, retry and others.

STEP 1 - three small edits to ringer_core/central_evidence.py, with tests added to tests/test_central_evidence.py:
 a. connect(credentials, autocommit: bool = False): pass autocommit through to psycopg.connect. Existing behavior for the default is unchanged.
 b. resolve_source_host(configured: str | None = None) -> str: returns the configured value stripped if it is non-empty, otherwise socket.gethostname().split(".", 1)[0], and if that is empty returns "unknown-host".
 c. stamp(): treat a missing, None or empty-string logged_at as absent (today only a missing key counts).

STEP 2 - rewrite EvalLogger in ringer.py with this behavior:
 - __init__(config): unchanged signature. Keep self._conn, self._fallback_path, self._fallback_reason and the existing attribute names (a test assigns logger._conn directly). When config.backend == "postgres", connect as before, but build credentials with central_evidence.resolve_credentials(parse_env_file(config.postgres.env_file)) and open the connection with central_evidence.connect(credentials, autocommit=True). A ValueError from resolve_credentials, a RuntimeError from connect (psycopg missing) or any other connect exception sets self._fallback_reason to a message that starts with "postgres " (for example "postgres connect failed: <exc>", "postgres config missing", or the ValueError text) and leaves self._conn None. The word "Supabase" must not appear anywhere inside the EvalLogger class (an automated check greps for it).
 - log_attempt(row): (1) compute source_host = central_evidence.resolve_source_host(config.postgres.source_host if config.postgres else None) and spec_storage = config.postgres.spec_storage if config.postgres else "hash". (2) logged_at = the row's own logged_at if present else datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(); use that ONE value for both sinks. (3) If self._conn is not None: build params with central_evidence.to_params(dict(row, logged_at=logged_at), source_host, spec_storage) and call self._conn.execute(central_evidence.INSERT_SQL, params); on success log_sink is "postgres" and fallback_reason is None for this row; on ANY exception set self._fallback_reason = f"postgres insert failed: {exc}", close the connection (set self._conn None via _close_conn), emit the one-time warning (below), and log_sink is "jsonl". (4) ALWAYS append the JSONL row via append_jsonl to self._fallback_path: the row's own keys exactly as today, plus logged_at, log_sink and fallback_reason. The JSONL row must NOT gain source_host, attempt_uid or spec_sha256 (record shape is preserved; a later `evidence push` recomputes identity from logged_at). The local JSONL keeps the full spec text exactly as before.
 - fallback_reason for rows after a failure keeps the earlier reason (existing behavior); for rows that reach Postgres it is None.
 - If append_jsonl raises, the exception propagates exactly as today (the central insert, if any, has already happened).
 - One-time warning: the first time the logger enters a fallback because of a connect or insert problem while config.backend == "postgres" (or a connection was injected), print exactly one line to sys.stderr: f"ringer: central evidence write failed ({reason}); attempt rows are still saved to {jsonl_path}". Never print it twice for the same logger instance, and never print it for the plain jsonl backend.
 - close(): unchanged behavior.
 - Rows for the plain "jsonl" backend with no connection must be identical in shape to today: the row's keys plus logged_at, log_sink "jsonl", fallback_reason None.

STEP 3 - tests:
 - Rewrite tests/test_model_log.py::test_postgres_params_exclude_local_model_log_keys (rename it test_postgres_params_include_all_attempt_columns). Keep its FakeConn with execute(sql, params) and `logger._conn = fake`. Assert: sql == central_evidence.INSERT_SQL; the params key set equals set(central_evidence.ATTEMPT_COLUMNS); model, task_type, retry and reasoning_effort ARE present with the row's values; spec is None and spec_sha256 is set (default hash policy); and a JSONL row was also written with log_sink "postgres". Change nothing else in that file.
 - Create tests/test_eval_logger_central.py with a fake psycopg injected through sys.modules (and removed afterward) covering: success dual-writes and both rows share logged_at; params carry source_host from config and from the default hostname; attempt_uid equals central_evidence.attempt_uid(source_host, jsonl_row); spec_storage "excerpt" keeps the spec text centrally; an insert failure falls back, sets a reason starting "postgres insert failed", closes the connection, still writes JSONL with log_sink "jsonl" and that reason, and prints exactly one stderr line (capture stderr; send two more rows and assert still one line); a connect failure and a missing-psycopg case (sys.modules["psycopg"] = None) fall back with a "postgres" reason, one warning, JSONL written; missing database settings fall back with the "missing database settings" text; the plain jsonl backend prints nothing to stderr and its row shape has no source_host/attempt_uid/spec_sha256; JSONL write failure propagates (patch append_jsonl to raise OSError) after a successful central insert.
 - Add the tests for the three central_evidence.py edits.

HOW TO RUN (from the repo root; fix failures inside your owned files only):
  cd /home/powerbox2/src/ringer-worktrees/shared-evidence && RINGER_NO_SELF_UPDATE=1 python3 -m unittest tests.test_eval_logger_central tests.test_central_evidence tests.test_model_log -v
  cd /home/powerbox2/src/ringer-worktrees/shared-evidence && python3 specs/002-shared-evidence/dispatch/check_t004.py
The second command runs the full suite (it tolerates only the known pre-existing contributor-credit failure), verifies your ringer.py diff stays inside EvalLogger, and drives the real EvalLogger end to end with a fake psycopg; it must print PASS. Read its failure lines carefully: they say exactly what differs.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: the owned files changed as described, plus ./notes.md in the scratch directory listing what you read, what you changed, the commands that passed, and any assumption. HARD RULES: never edit outside your owned files or outside EvalLogger in ringer.py; do not change any other existing test; if an existing test other than test_postgres_params_exclude_local_model_log_keys fails because of your change, fix your change, not the test; if a requirement is ambiguous choose the reading that makes check_t004.py pass and record it in notes.md.
